title: Writing a paragraph in German
subtitle: How to write a short paragraph about everyday life at A1–A2 — what the grader looks for and how to deliver it.

text.text: Every attempt is scored on four criteria. You get a score for each one, plus corrections of your sentences. Knowing the four criteria tells you where to spend your effort.
— did you answer the question, include every required element, and stay inside the word range?
— do your sentences come in a clear order, joined with simple connectors such as "and", "but" and "because"?
— did you use words that fit the topic, spelled correctly, without repeating the same word again and again?
— are your verb forms, agreement and word order correct?
30–60 words, 10 minutes on the timer.
60–100 words, 15 minutes on the timer.
Writing fewer words than the minimum costs you on Task achievement, even if every sentence is correct.

Here is a model paragraph on the topic
(my weekend), one sentence at a time. It is 75 words — A2 length. At A1, write the opening, two supporting sentences and the closing.

target.text: Am Wochenende habe ich viel Zeit für meine Familie

body.en: At the weekend I have a lot of time for my family and my hobbies.

note.text: Opening sentence: says what the paragraph is about. The time phrase comes first, so the verb

target.text: Am Samstag stehe ich spät auf

body.en: On Saturday I get up late and have breakfast with my brother.

target.text: gehen wir zusammen in den Park,

body.en: Then we go to the park together, because we like playing football.

target.text: Am Abend koche ich oft für meine Freunde,

body.en: In the evening I often cook for my friends, and sometimes we also go to the cinema.

target.text: am Nachmittag lese ich ein Buch.

body.en: On Sunday I first visit my grandparents, and in the afternoon I read a book.
I like the weekend a lot, but it is always too short!

note.text: Closing sentence: your feeling about the topic.

text.text: Notice that each sentence does one job, and the highlighted connectors link them. Starting sentences with a time phrase (
) gives the paragraph a clear order — just remember the verb still comes second.
Connectors are the small words that show how one idea relates to the next. At this level, a handful used correctly is enough.

items.en: I play the guitar and I also like singing.

text.text: German has two ways to say "you". Use
with friends, family and children; use
with adults you do not know, with people in an official role (a teacher, a doctor, a landlord) and in formal letters.
is always written with a capital S, and its verb form is the same as for
(they).

body.en: Do you have time on Saturday?
Do you have time on Saturday?

sections.title: the task and the word count

text.text: Most prompts list
— things your text must mention. The grader checks each one. Make every element visibly present: give it its own sentence, and use the element's own key word so it cannot be missed.

target.text: Am Sonntag esse ich mit meiner Familie zu Mittag.

body.en: On Sunday I have lunch with my family.

note.text: Required element "what you do on Sunday" — the sentence starts with the key word

text.text: Before you write, list the required elements and give each one a sentence. Add your opening and closing sentence to the plan.
Short, correct sentences score better than long sentences with mistakes.

Add a reason (with "because") or an example to one of your points.
Cut repetition first — sentences that say the same thing twice — not a required element.
These are the errors the grader flags most often at A1–A2. Each example shows the
sentence; the wrong version is in the note.

target.text: Am Montag gehe ich ins Kino.

body.en: On Monday I go to the cinema.

note.text: not: *Am Montag ich gehe ins Kino*. In a main clause the verb is always the second element, even when the sentence starts with a time phrase.

target.text: Ich bleibe zu Hause, weil ich krank bin.

body.en: I am staying at home because I am ill.

note.text: the verb goes to the end.

target.text: Die Wohnung ist klein, aber der Balkon ist groß.

body.en: The flat is small, but the balcony is big.

note.text: not: *Der Wohnung … die Balkon*. Learn every noun with its article:

target.text: Ich stehe um sieben Uhr auf.

body.en: I get up at seven o'clock.

note.text: not: *Ich aufstehe um sieben Uhr*. In a main clause, separable verbs split: the prefix goes to the end of the clause. After
(or a modal verb) the verb stays in one piece at the end:

children.text: …, weil ich um sieben Uhr aufstehe

body.en: In the evening I read a book.
